title: Quentin and the Locker
premise: Petra Dunmore, a scholarship student counting down the days to graduation at Ashgrove Academy, is paired for a semester project with her nemesis Quentin Hale — the headmaster's son who once ruined her scholarship interview. Digging into the school's archives for their assignment, they discover a locker sealed since 1998 and the paper trail of a scandal the school board buried: a student's expulsion that covered up negligence in a fire. As Petra and Quentin's uneasy alliance deepens into loyalty, she must choose between protecting the boy she's come to trust and publishing the truth before prom. In the end, she exposes the board at prom itself, Quentin publicly sides with her against his father, and Petra walks out of graduation not just free, but finally belonging to herself.
about_author: Ines Voss is a former boarding school teacher who spent six years listening to secrets echo down dormitory hallways before turning them into fiction. She writes young adult novels about institutional silence and the teenagers loud enough to break it.

chapters.title: Days Remaining
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Opening with her countdown calendar to graduation, we see Ashgrove through her wary eyes: the wealth, the unwritten rules, her scholarship precariousness. A humiliating hallway collision with Quentin Hale reopens old wounds from her botched freshman interview. Emotional beat: resentment sharpened by exhaustion — she just wants to survive to June.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Mr. Okafor announces semester-long paired capstone projects; Petra draws Quentin. Their first meeting in the library is pure friction until he suggests researching the school's founding era and she notices a gap in the archive index — a missing year, 1998. Emotional beat: reluctant truce, curiosity overriding hatred.

chapters.title: The Sealed Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Exploring the east wing basement, they find locker 114, welded shut, its number absent from every registry. Quentin recognizes his father's handwriting on an old maintenance order. Petra realizes he's shaken — this isn't a game to him either. Emotional beat: unease curdling into shared purpose.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He breaks into his father's home office and finds a 1998 disciplinary file: Marisol Vega, expelled days after a chemistry lab fire that injured three students. The official report blames her; a suppressed inspection blames faulty ventilation the board refused to fund. Emotional beat: guilt — his family built their name on the lie.

chapters.title: Allies and Alibis
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They track down Marisol, now a nurse two towns over, who confirms everything but begs them to let it go — the settlement bought her silence and her mother's medical care. Petra, whose own future depends on Ashgrove's goodwill, understands the bargain too well. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made personal.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Headmaster Hale grows suspicious of Quentin's archive requests and quietly moves to revoke Petra's scholarship on fabricated conduct charges. Her friends distance themselves; her countdown calendar becomes a deadline. She and Quentin agree: publish everything before prom night, when the whole board will be in one room. Emotional beat: isolation forging resolve.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Using a maintenance key Quentin steals, they open the locker: inside are Marisol's confiscated lab notes, the original inspection report, and letters from injured students' families that were never answered. Someone catches them — Mr. Okafor, who reveals he was the young teacher who reported the hazards and was silenced. Emotional beat: grief and vindication intertwined.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Headmaster Hale confronts his son privately: full tuition anywhere, a clean record, his father's blessing — if the documents disappear. Quentin, who has spent his life earning approval that never comes, nearly accepts. Petra finds him holding the folder over a burn barrel. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth embodied in one trembling choice.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Under the gymnasium lights, as the board gathers onstage, Petra takes the microphone during the senior speech slot and reads the 1998 inspection aloud while Okafor distributes copies and Marisol stands at the back, witnessed at last. Hale lunges to cut the power; Quentin steps between him and the projector. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Weeks later: the board resigns, Marisol's record is cleared, and Okafor becomes interim headmaster. Petra's scholarship is reinstated — but she's already been accepted elsewhere on merit alone. She and Quentin part at the gates not as nemesis or allies but as equals. She throws away the countdown calendar. Emotional beat: quiet, earned freedom.
